questions.prompt: How should lock-activity notifications be delivered?
questions.description: When a recognized user uses the keypad, where does the notification go? Multiple channels can be combined.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Send via a configurable HA notify action (e.g. notify.mobile_app_* or notify.notify, set in app settings) plus keep an in-app activity log. Persistent notifications are optional, not default.

questions.prompt: Which lock events should trigger a notification for a recognized user?
questions.description: Z2M reports keypad unlock/lock with the user slot that was used. Manual operations have no user.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Notify on keypad unlock AND keypad lock by a recognized user (slot mapped to a name). Manual/unknown operations are logged in the activity feed but not notified.

questions.prompt: How should PINs be stored in the app database?
questions.description: Z2M requires expose_pin: true anyway, so PINs already travel over MQTT. Storage choices affect what the UI can re-display.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Store PINs encrypted at rest (key generated and stored in /data). Admin can reveal a stored PIN on demand in the UI. PINs are never written to logs or debug output.

questions.prompt: How should the app stay in sync with the lock's actual user codes?
questions.description: Reading all slots over Zigbee can be slow/flaky (per-slot MQTT queries). Writes can be verified by reading back the affected slot.
questions.recommendedAnswer: On-demand: a Refresh button per lock re-reads slots (with per-slot timeouts and graceful fallback to cached state), and every PIN write is verified by reading back that slot. No periodic full sync in v1.

options.label: Periodic full sync of all slots
Write-only, app DB is source of truth

questions.prompt: How should locks be discovered/added in the app?
questions.description: HA's device registry knows which lock entities belong to Zigbee2MQTT devices; the friendly name is also the Z2M MQTT base topic.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Auto-detect Zigbee2MQTT lock entities via the HA device registry (websocket), let the user pick which to manage. No manual entity entry in v1.

questions.prompt: How do users relate to locks?
questions.description: A slot+name list could be per lock, or global users could be mapped to the same slot across multiple locks.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Per-lock user lists for v1 (each lock has its own slot→name mapping). Global users across locks is a future feature.

questions.prompt: If a PIN write fails (lock offline, Z2M timeout), what should happen?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Show a clear error in the UI with the slot marked as unsynced; user retries manually. No automatic retry queue in v1.

questions.prompt: How will you install/distribute the app?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Own GitHub repository with repository.yaml; multi-arch images (amd64+aarch64) built and published to GHCR via GitHub Actions; install by adding the repo URL in HA's App Store.

questions.prompt: Confirm what is explicitly OUT of scope for v1 (kept for later).
questions.description: Keep v1 small: users (slot, name), set PIN, notify on activity. Select everything that should NOT be in v1.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All listed items are out of scope for v1: no date/time schedules, no global users across locks, no auto-retry queue, no per-user notification routing or message templates.
